name: Electronic USD
oneLiner: EUSD is a Reserve Protocol RToken backed by a basket of yield-bearing Aave and Compound USDC/USDT lending positions, with RSR stakers as first-loss buffer.
collateral: Diversified basket of yield-bearing stablecoin derivatives: Aave V3 USDC, Compound V3 USDC, and Compound V3 USDT; RSR stakers provide first-loss overcollateralization
pegMechanism: Permissionless 1:1 mint and redemption against underlying collateral basket; RSR stakers absorb first losses in case of collateral default; basket rebalances via Dutch/batch auctions

applicabilityBasis.summary: Electronic USD is a Reserve Protocol RToken with on-chain basket collateral and governance rather than a legal fiat issuer.

genius.issuerEntity: Electronic Dollar governance / Reserve Protocol RToken governors
genius.notes: eUSD is stablecoin-adjacent but protocol-governed; no public GENIUS approval or issuer pathway source was found. The payment use case via RPay (Latin America) makes applicability genuinely unclear rather than a clean non-payment-token exclusion.

No GENIUS approvals have been granted to any issuer as of 2026-06-07; rulemaking remains at NPRM stage.

mintAuthority.summary: EUSD is a Reserve Protocol RToken: anyone can permissionlessly mint 1:1 by depositing the collateral basket (Aave/Compound USDC and USDT positions) and redeem for the basket, with RSR stakers as first-loss buffer; the per-RToken Governor + 7-day TimelockController controls basket and parameter changes.

controls.label: RToken contract (permissionless basket mint)
controls.capDescription: Mint is 1:1 against the current collateral basket only; supply is bounded by deposited collateral, with arbitrage holding the peg.
controls.evidence: RTokens are minted by depositing the basket and redeemed for the basket; eUSD's basket is Aave/Compound USDC and USDT positions, so minting is bounded by deposited collateral.

controls.label: eUSD Governor + TimelockController (basket governance)
controls.evidence: Each RToken is governed by its own RSR-staker Governor paired with a TimelockController; basket changes require a minimum ~7-day delay. Reserve factory contracts are immutable and not upgradeable.

review.evidence: Reserve docs describe eUSD as a permissionless basket-mint RToken backed by Aave/Compound deposits with RSR first-loss staking; basket/parameter changes run through a per-RToken Governor + ~7-day TimelockController, while factory contracts are immutable.
review.sourceFreeRationale: Permissionless basket-mint + timelock governance model confirmed from Reserve docs; exact eUSD Governor/Timelock addresses and current quorum not independently read on-chain.
unresolvedQuestions: Resolve the deployed eUSD Governor and TimelockController addresses and the exact timelock delay/quorum on-chain.
